summary.text: Amino acids are organic compounds that contain both an amino group and a carboxylic acid group.
Over 500 exist in nature, but the 22 that appear in the genetic code are the ones built into proteins.
As parts of proteins, amino acid residues make up the second-largest component of human muscle and other tissues, after water.

facts.label: Last common one found
facts.value: Threonine, found in 1935 by William Cumming Rose

facts.label: Protein-building
facts.value: 22 of the many hundreds described are proteinogenic

facts.label: Handedness in proteins
facts.value: Chiral proteinogenic ones all have the L configuration

facts.label: Charged at neutral pH
facts.value: Five of them carry a charge

items.prompt: Histidine often takes part in proton transfers during enzyme reactions. What makes it suited to that?

options.label: It is the only amino acid fully protonated at pH 7
It is easily found in both its basic and acid forms
It carries a negative charge at neutral pH
It has no side chain that can change charge

items.explain: Histidine is easily found in its basic and conjugate acid forms, so it often joins catalytic proton transfers.

items.prompt: Chiral amino acids built into proteins all share one handedness. Which?

options.label: Right-handed, the D configuration
An even mix of both
Left-handed, the L configuration
Alternating along the chain

items.explain: All chiral proteinogenic amino acids have the L configuration, the left-handed form.

items.prompt: Glycine's side chain is just a hydrogen atom. What does that mean for its α-carbon?

options.label: It is not stereogenic, unlike in the others
It carries a charge at neutral pH
It carries two carboxyl groups
It is stereogenic like the others

items.explain: Except for glycine, whose side chain is also a hydrogen atom, the α-carbon is stereogenic.

items.prompt: Charged side chains often sit on the outside surface of a protein. What does that help the protein do?

options.label: Bind to ribosomes more tightly
Resist damage from UV light
Switch the handedness of its amino acids
Dissolve in the surrounding water

items.explain: Charged side chains often appear at protein surfaces to enable their solubility in water.

items.prompt: In 1902 two chemists proposed how amino acids link into proteins. Which parts of two neighbouring amino acids bond?

options.label: The amino group of one and the carboxyl group of the next
The side chain of one and the side chain of the next
The carboxyl groups of both, joined back to back
The amino groups of both, joined back to back

items.explain: Fischer and Hofmeister proposed that bonds form between the amino group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another, giving a linear chain.

items.prompt: Pepsin is an enzyme in the stomach, a very sour, low-pH place. Which residues may act as acids in it?

options.label: Arginine or lysine
Serine or threonine
Glycine or leucine
Aspartate or glutamate

items.explain: Enzymes in very low pH environments, like pepsin in the stomach, may have catalytic aspartate or glutamate residues that act as acids.
